facts.text: Serve the mains when Brantley changes from mailroom clothes to his suit in the lift.
facts.why: He does keep changing clothes to switch between mailroom boy and executive Carlton Whitfield. Neither Wikipedia nor the reviews I opened say he changes in an elevator.
facts.fix: Serve the mains when Brantley first walks onto the executive floor as Carlton Whitfield.

facts.text: Lean times call for a proper lunch. Charges go to your department. Elevators are not changing rooms.
facts.why: The note is signed Howard Prescott. The elevator changing room line depends on the elevator scene, which no opened source confirms. The rest suits the takeover plot.
facts.fix: Lean times call for a proper lunch. Charges go to your department. Nobody eats in the mailroom.

vibe.verdict: A smart executive dining room with a good routing slip, but it leaves out the quick changes and the bedroom pile up.
missing: Changing clothes between mailroom and executive floor (Brantley's double life)
The poolside seduction by Vera (his aunt by marriage)
The corporate party bedroom pile up (Brantley, Christy, Vera, Howard)
Christy at the water fountain (executive floor)

Swap 'Gin martini' for a pool deck cocktail named for Vera.
